alice: FYI escalation from ACME (ticket INC-2026-042). They flipped model quantization to int8 last night and started seeing p95/p99 latency regressions and occasional 500s. Customer says tail latency went from ~480ms p99 to ~2.1s p99. We're live on hosted-api, model redwood-3b-int8 (deployment id: dep-82f4). Logs attached below.

alice: top-level symptom: request success rate dropped from 99.9% -> 97.2% during peak, p50 unchanged (~90ms) but p95 up ~450ms -> 1.2s and p99 up ~480ms -> 2.1s. Happens with sequence lengths > 512 and batching enabled (auto-batch, target_batch=8). Customer observed regressions after enabling "quant_profile: int8" in their deployment config. They reverted to fp16 and p99 went back to normal.

alice: relevant excerpt from runtime logs on node gpu-17:
```
[2026-02-28T01:12:11Z] kernel_selector WARN: selected fallback kernel path for int8_gemm: slower_emulation_kernel
[2026-02-28T01:12:11Z] backend INFO: kvcache hit rate 72% prefix_len=128
[2026-02-28T01:12:12Z] request 0x7f3a: schedule -> batch_size=6 seq_len=1024 estimated_tokens=640
[2026-02-28T01:12:12Z] perf WARN: dynamic_quant calibration mismatch -> NaNs in qparams, falling back to fp16
[2026-02-28T01:12:12Z] request 0x7f3a: emit latency 2142ms
```

bob (eng-infra): Can you attach the exact deployment config (the customer's JSON) and the incident window timeframe? Need GPU metrics (util, mem_bandwidth) and host-side CPU spikes. Also which runtime version? We had a change to kernel selection in runtime v1.18.2.

alice: timeframe: 2026-02-28 01:10:00 -> 01:25:00 UTC. Runtime: 1.18.2-hotfix. Customer config (redacted API key):
```
{
  "model": "redwood-3b-int8",
  "quant_profile": "int8",
  "batching": { "mode": "auto", "target_batch": 8, "max_latency_ms": 50 },
  "fallback": { "enabled": true, "order": ["fp16"] }
}
```

carlos (eng-runtime): Thanks — initial read: two likely compounding issues:
- quant calibration produced unstable qparams (NaNs) for long sequences -> runtime emits a fallback but that code path isn't optimized and forces slower kernels + extra memory copies. That explains p99 impact while p50 stays fine.
- kernel_selector recently changed heuristics in v1.18.2 and will pick a slower_emulation_kernel when it detects poor quantization stats. We have a ticket for tuning but not shipped.

carlos: Quick repro steps (local) to validate tail behavior:
1) Checkout runtime v1.18.2
2) Start local dev runtime with --enable-quant --verbose-kernel-select
3) Use model weights converted with int8 profile and use a synthetic input with seq_len=1024

Example run (bash):
```
# spin up runtime
./redwood-runtime --port 8080 --runtime-version 1.18.2 --enable-quant --gpu 0

# stress test
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -H "x-debug: kernels,quant" -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-3b-int8","input":"$(python3 -c "print('a '*600)")"}' &
done
```

dani (eng-ml): adding ML context — calibration failing (NaNs) is often caused by outlier activations during per-channel min/max collection or a bad calibration dataset (too short, was mostly padding). The quantizer then emits extreme scales causing unstable int8 GEMM. In such cases the runtime's dynamic fallback to fp16 keeps correctness but performance suffers.

dani: mitigation options:
- Re-run calibration with a representative dataset (no heavy padding, include long context examples). Use our calibration tool with --clip 0.999 and --per-channel.
- Enable a conservative quant_profile: "int8_safe" (we have an internal profile that clamps scales and disables asymmetric per-tensor quant for LLaMA-like layers).
- If immediate mitigation needed: set fallback order to ["fp16"] and set a policy to disable batching for sequences > 512 so we don't hit batching-induced kernel slow-paths.

eve (customer-success): Customer asks for step-by-step to be able to rollback safely if we push changes. They prefer us to coordinate a canary that targets 10% of traffic and rollback automatically on p99 > 1s.

carlos: Proposed immediate mitigations to reduce customer impact (ordered):
1) Patch runtime config for their deployment (server-side) to force quant fallback to fp16 early for seq_len > 512. Config change:
```
{"quant_policy": {"force_fallback_seq_len_gt": 512, "fallback_order": ["fp16"], "prefer_fast_gemm": true}}
```
2) Reduce target_batch to 4 for that deployment while we validate kernels.
3) Canary a runtime change that prefers the older kernel-selector heuristic for int8 until we tune the new heuristics.
4) Re-run calibration with ACME-provided example payloads; if calibration succeeds, promote int8 with conservative profile.

bob: I'll schedule an emergency job to patch their deployment. Need someone from eng-ml to run calibration with ACME dataset. Also need a canary checklist (metrics to watch):
- API errors (5xx rate)
- p50/p95/p99 latencies
- GPU util, sm_efficiency, mem_bw
- kernel_selector warnings count
- kvcache hit rate

dani: I'm on calibration. Please get me a small sample of 200 representative requests (anonymized). I'll run the calibration tool and post results here.

alice: ACME shared 230 anonymized requests (attached). I uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/inc-2026-042/acme-calib.tar.gz

carlos: After today's quick patch we should also add telemetry: emit quant_calib_status per-deployment and a histogram of selected kernel types per model so support can triage quickly.

deploy-bot: deploy start dep-82f4 -> patch quant_policy (user-scoped) by ops at 2026-02-28T02:05:00Z

ops (operator): Patch applied to dep-82f4: target_batch=4, quant_policy.force_fallback_seq_len_gt=512. Canary 10% traffic.

metrics-bot: Canary metrics (first 30m): p99 dropped from 2.1s -> 620ms; 5xx rate back to 99.4% success. Kernel_selector warnings reduced by 80%.

alice: Customer confirmed tail latency improvement. They still want a durable fix (full int8 w/o regressions) because int8 reduces cost ~28%.

carlos: Long-term action items:
- eng-runtime: revert/tune kernel_selector heuristics and add a fast fallback path for emulation kernels.
- eng-ml: ship a robust "int8_safe" quant profile and improve calibration tool docs (include instructions for long seqs and padding-aware sampling).
- platform: include quant_calib_status and kernel histogram in Console and alerting runbooks.

alice: Assigning owners: eng-runtime (carlos) -> kernel selector tuning, eng-ml (dani) -> int8_safe and calibration docs, platform (bob) -> telemetry and canary automation. I'll update INC-2026-042 and inform ACME of timeline (ETA: patch tests + canary tomorrow morning UTC).

eve: ACME thanks everyone for quick response. They requested weekly status updates until full int8 rollout.

alice: closing note: if anyone sees similar escalations, check these quick signals first: kernel_selector WARN entries, "dynamic_quant calibration mismatch", and whether seq_len distribution is skewed >512. Those are strong indicators quantization is the cause.

alice: marking thread resolved for now; will re-open if canary regresses.
